correctness.rationale: PASS. I reconstructed the graph metric on 2n vertices with outer step one, spokes, inner step three; n>=19 gives girth six because a spoke-containing short cycle must solve +/-a+/-3b=0 with a+b<=4, which forces a=3,b=1. Its n hexagons share outer edges, each inner edge is private. The unique common neighbor for every distance-two pair identifies 2n centered tetrahedra. The explicit radius-two-ball triple intersections show exactly 2n maximal noncentered triangles (two alternating triples per hexagon) and no higher noncentered clique. Independent graph-square clique enumeration gave the full face vector, exact noncentered triangle sets, and no extraneous tetrahedra for n=19,20,21,22,24,27. For each center the tetrahedron/top-neighbor-triangle then three centered triangles/distance-two-edges collapse, totaling 8n free-face pairs and leaving the original graph. Each pair of exceptional triangles becomes two disks on the same length-six loop; private inner edges cancel one disk per hexagon, leaving the outer circle, while other disks form n spherical wedges. The inner-edge coefficients of the hexagon loops give a primitive integral sublattice. The join-of-three-0-spheres octahedral cycles have integral boundary zero and are the paired-disk differences; explicit chain permutation calculation at n=19 gave rotation z_i->z_{i+1}, reflection z_i->z_{-i-3} with positive sign, consistent with the uniform orientation argument. Independently computed n=18 boundary F2 ranks (35,127,36), f=(36,162,186,36), beta~=(0,0,23,0). Finite checks do not establish the all-n theorem; the uniform clique/attachment proof supplies that step.
